                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q10.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> During the mobility, your institution fosters the integration of the incoming mobile participants</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The institution appoints responsible person(s) to deal with practical issues (e.g. social, health, and/or psychological problems)</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The institution should ensure there are named, visible persons who are responsible for the practical issues associated with integrating mobile students. This visibility should be ensured through introduction to this function during the Welcome / Orientation period and be detailed on the website so all mobile students can easily access this support, throughout their stay.&nbsp;</p><p>Non-academic mentoring and support arrangements should already be outlined in the Course Catalogue of the receiving HEI, in the section on general information for students, with relevant contact persons in the respective areas. Academic advisors should have close contact with the practical services which are available to incoming participants as they are often the first line of contact to the incoming student. Further information sessions should be arranged for all staff who work with incoming students to ensure they are adequately signposted on to the appropriate services they require.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It appoints responsible person(s) to deal with academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.)</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is important that the receiving institution appoints specific named academic advisors who are responsible for dealing with problems related to academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.) of incoming students.&nbsp; Information on mentoring for thesis writing for incoming students is particularly important and clear mentoring arrangements should be agreed upon between the student, sending and receiving institutions and organised before the mobility.</p><p>For traineeships, a mentor, different from the supervisor, should be nominated to support and encourage the mobile student while in the receiving organisation. The mentor should also provide information on the culture of the enterprise and informal codes and conducts, of the receiving organisation. The contact details of both the supervisor and the mentor should be specified in the Learning Agreement.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises Welcome / Orientation activities at the beginning of each semester</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>An important aspect of the support arrangement is the welcome or orientation activities. These welcome / orientation activities should provide the incoming students with the necessary information on practical and administrative arrangements, to allow incoming students to meet local and other mobile students, to introduce the learning and teaching methods of the receiving institution, academic regulations, the institutional culture, health and safety issues. These activities should address any type of concern of the incoming student, and reduce any psychological pressure they might feel during their first contacts at the receiving institution. The welcome&nbsp; / orientation activities should be designed to take into account any cultural and religious sensitivities of the incoming students (ensuring a range of activities to suit different types of students).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises activities to integrate them in the receiving institution and the local community, e.g. with the support of student organisations, Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association etc.</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>As well as academic and practical support from the institution, incoming students need to feel fully integrated into the student community, something which is best done by their fellow students / peers. Local student association(s), such as Erasmus Student Network (ESN) and the other associations’ member of the ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>), play an important role in supporting incoming students. Incoming students need to feel welcomed and included in the student organisations. To help this process, the student organisations need to be aware of their role in supporting this integration and have access to the right resources, information, guidance and incentives. As institutions often have many types of student organisations, cooperation between them is encouraged through meetings together, social activities and buddy programmes. A key aspect of these activities is to make sure they are for all students so incoming students are integrated with the local students and hence the culture. Student organisations include for example, ESN (Erasmus Student Network) or ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>). ESAA runs a buddy system to encourage integration of incoming students with their peers inside the institution and share good practice with other member associations around Europe.</p>                      </div>

                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> At the end of the mobility, your institution has formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to recognition at the end of the mobility, e.g. in the use of Transcripts of Records and Grade Distribution Tables)</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records are issued in a timely manner (normally 5 weeks) to both incoming and outgoing students</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important in the recognition framework to provide Transcripts of Records in a timely manner, immediately following the mobility period. After the mobility, the receiving institution should send a Transcript of Records to the student and to the sending institution within a period stipulated in the Inter-Institutional Agreement (normally within five weeks after publication/proclamation of the student’s results at the receiving institution). It can be provided electronically or through any other means accessible to the student and the sending institution. The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should refer to the educational components agreed upon in the Learning Agreement. Grade distribution information should be included as well, either as a web link or an annex.</p><p>Following the receipt of the Transcript of Records from the receiving institution, the sending institution should automatically transfer and recognise the student’s academic outcomes successfully completed at the receiving institution, as agreed in the Learning Agreement, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The Sending Institution will provide a Transcript of Records to the student or record the results in a database or any other means accessible to the student, normally within five weeks after having received the transcript of the receiving institution. The EU official template for the Learning Agreement for studies (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All credits gained by students during a period of study abroad that were specified in the final version of the Learning Agreement are automatically transferred by your institution and count towards the students' final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The sending institution should ensure that all the credits earned by the mobile student during the mobility period are recognised and counted towards the final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The period of study abroad must be clear in the student's records and documents issued to the student (Diploma Supplement or equivalent). This is a golden rule of recognition of credit mobility within the framework of inter-institutional agreements. All the credits towards the student's degree that are earned during the mobility period and which were originally agreed on in the Learning Agreement (or a revised version to it) should be recognised by the sending HEI without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. Learning Agreements are binding for all the parties and require that, on successful completion of the mobility period, the sending HEI recognises credits earned by the student and documents these credits in the student records, so they can be identified in a transparent way.</p><p>Upon receipt of the Transcript of Records or Training Certificates, the sending HEI should:<br>a) certify the mobile student has fulfilled all requirements stipulated in the Learning Agreement;<br>b) ensure recognition of the mobility period abroad within the time-scale and according to the conditions stipulated in the institutional recognition framework.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include a description of or a link to the national grading system</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should include grade distribution information, either as a web link or an annex. The local grading scale should be clearly explained, with a statistical distribution of local grades, to provide transparency and understanding of grading practices at the host institution. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility. There are more details on this in the ECTS Users’ Guide.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">In addition to recognising formal learning, the institution recognises any non-formal or informal learning acquired during the mobility according to the ECTS Users’ Guide, e.g. by awarding ECTS credits for volunteering</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>During a period of mobility, students often take advantage of other opportunities outside of their required courses. These may include specific activities which can be considered non-formal or informal learning where they have acquired new skills. This could include additional language and cultural courses, extra-curricular activities, setting up a business and volunteer work undertaken by the student in that period or upon return at the receiving institution.</p>                      </div>

                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution issues a Diploma Supplement</div>

                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>

                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-mobility-supporting-individuals-development-and-institutional-aims-and-objectives" target="_blank">Recognition of staff mobility – supporting individuals’ development and institutional aims and objectives</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-participating-in-erasmus-staff-mobility-actions-and-international-cooperation-projects" target="_blank">Recognition of staff participating in Erasmus staff mobility actions and international cooperation projects</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-erasmus-impact-study-effects-of-mobility-on-the-skills-and-employability-of-students-and-the-internationalisation-of-higher-education-institutions" target="_blank">The Erasmus Impact Study: Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                     </div>
    </div>
</div>

About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

Senior Sales Regional Enterprise Manager

At Wolt, we create technology that brings local communities, merchants and customers closer together. What started with restaurant delivery has grown into a broader local commerce platform, helping customers discover and access more of what their cities have to offer.

As our Retail business continues to grow, we're looking for a Senior Sales Regional Enterprise Manager to expand our selection of high-value regional retail partners. You'll join our Sales team and take ownership of some of the most important regional acquisition opportunities across priority retail verticals, helping shape what customers can find on Wolt in their cities. This role can be based in Berlin, Cologne, Frankfurt, Hamburg or Munich .

What you'll be doing

In this role, you'll own the acquisition and development of high-value regional Enterprise retail partners in Germany, from identifying and engaging the right prospects through commercial negotiations, signing and initial rollout. You'll combine strong commercial execution with a strategic view on which partners can have the greatest impact on Wolt's selection, coverage and long-term growth.

Day-to-day in this role you'll:

  • Own the end-to-end sales cycle for regional Enterprise retail opportunities, from prospecting and qualification through negotiation, contracting and signing.
  • Build and manage a high-quality pipeline of larger regional retailers and multi-location partners across priority verticals such as grocery, convenience, pet, pharmacy and beauty.
  • Develop a deep understanding of prospective partners' businesses and create compelling commercial propositions that demonstrate the value of partnering with Wolt.
  • Lead complex commercial negotiations, balancing partner needs with sustainable economics and Wolt's long-term business objectives.
  • Build strong relationships with senior decision-makers and act as a trusted commercial partner throughout the sales process.
  • Work closely with internal teams including Operations, Account Management, Finance, Legal, Marketing and Product to structure partnerships and enable successful launches.
  • Take ownership beyond the signature, ensuring a strong handover and initial rollout so that newly acquired partners can successfully go live and scale.
  • Use market insights, pipeline data and commercial learnings to identify opportunities, prioritize the highest-impact accounts and continuously improve our regional Enterprise sales approach.
  • Contribute to sharing best practices and raising the bar for Enterprise sales execution across the wider team.

Our humble expectations

  • You have significant experience in B2B sales, business development or strategic partnerships, ideally working with Enterprise or other complex, multi-stakeholder customers.
  • You have a strong track record of independently managing and closing complex commercial opportunities from initial outreach through contract signature.
  • You're an excellent negotiator and understand how to build partnerships that create sustainable value for both sides.
  • You're comfortable engaging and influencing senior stakeholders, both externally and across cross-functional internal teams.
  • You combine a hands-on, results-oriented sales mindset with strong commercial judgment and the ability to prioritize opportunities based on their strategic impact.
  • You're highly structured and comfortable managing multiple opportunities and stakeholders simultaneously while maintaining strong attention to detail.
  • You're comfortable working with data and commercial metrics to evaluate opportunities, build business cases and inform decisions.
  • You communicate clearly and persuasively and are fluent in German and English. 

What we offer

This is an opportunity to play a meaningful role in the next phase of Wolt's Retail growth. You'll have direct ownership of high-impact regional partnerships and the autonomy to take opportunities from first conversation all the way through to launch.

You'll work at the intersection of sales, strategy and operations, collaborating with experienced colleagues across Wolt while building relationships with some of the most important retailers in the market. The role offers substantial commercial ownership and exposure while giving you the opportunity to develop further in Enterprise sales and contribute to how we scale our Retail business.

You'll also join a fast-moving international environment where good ideas can quickly turn into action, with the tools, support and trust to take ownership of your work and make a visible impact.

Next steps

If this sounds like an opportunity you'd be excited about, we'd love to hear from you.

Description

Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale.

We set the standard for AI-powered contract work by offering a platform that changes how legal teams work, from drafting through negotiation to completion. We are now looking for the person who turns what customers actually need into what our AI actually does.

Joining Legartis is not taking a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and lawyers, who do not chase hype; we build substance. If you are a lawyer who builds, someone who has stopped waiting for better tools and started making them, this is your moment and your place.

Send us your CV, a short note on why Legartis, and links to anything you have built or published.


Your mission

Most companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you.

1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first "wow" moment themselves. When they say "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against.

2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on.

3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not.

4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough.


Your profile

The person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not "lawyer who is good with computers". It is legal quant: a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster.

A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job.

If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold.

1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus.

2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer.

3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why "they did not understand the value" is never the customer's fault. If instead you have supported enterprise sales teams in demos, pilots, and expert calls, tell us what you changed about the outcome.

You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter.

4. Language. Excellent German and English. German is non-negotiable: our customers are DACH legal teams and the nuance lives in their language. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus.


Why us?

  • Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, product, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate.
  • No silos. You sit between Product, Engineering, and the customer, with a direct line to all three. The better argument wins, not the higher title.
  • We invest in you. The enterprise motion (multi-stakeholder pilots, procurement cycles, security reviews) is teachable, and we teach it: side by side in real customer calls from week one.
  • Real ownership. Competitive salary and employee stock options (ESOP).
  • Build in public. We want you to keep publishing what you build, because it makes you better and it makes us visible.
  • Offices in Berlin, Leipzig, and Zurich with a flexible hybrid setup. Regular apéros, lunches, and hiking trips as we enjoy the journey together.


Process

  1. Expectations. A conversation with the People Manager about the role and who you are.
  2. Depth. A conversation with our General Counsel & Head of Legal AI on Legal Engineering at Legartis and where the legal market is going.
  3. Build session. A live case at the intersection of legal reasoning, prompting, and product work: a real customer scenario, a legal AI workflow, or a playbook that misbehaves.

    Type: Full-time
    Location: University of Sussex, Brighton - On-site

    The Role

    Netholabs is building AI grounded in biological intelligence. We record petascale, high-resolution neurobehavioural data from living systems and use it to train neural foundation models — a new substrate for the next generation of AI, robotics, and personalised intelligence. We aim to greatly reduce the burden of animals used in basic scientific research and pharmacological work, with eventual removal and replacement by in silico models.

    We're looking for a Neuroscientist to join our Brighton research team as an independent contributor driving experiments from design through analysis. You'll design and run in vivo electrophysiology and behavioural experiments, work with large-scale neural and behavioural datasets, and partner closely with our ML team to translate what we learn about real brains and bodies into better foundation models. This is a role for someone who wants their science to feed directly into what gets built next.

    Responsibilities

    In Vivo Electrophysiology & Neural Recording

    • Design and run in vivo electrophysiology experiments in animal models

    • Develop and refine neural recording protocols and rigs alongside the hardware team

    • Ensure recordings meet the quality and fidelity standards our models are trained on

    Behavioural Neuroscience & Experimental Design

    • Design behavioural paradigms that generate rich, well-controlled datasets

    • Plan and oversee data collection sessions, in collaboration with technicians

    • Iterate on experimental design based on data quality and downstream modelling needs

    Data Analysis & Computational Modelling

    • Analyse large-scale neural and behavioural datasets

    • Build and apply computational models to characterise neural and behavioural dynamics

    • Validate findings and communicate results clearly to the broader research team

    Neuroscience → AI Translation

    • Partner with the ML team to translate biological findings into model design choices

    • Help define what neurobehavioural data and features are most valuable to capture

    • Contribute to internal research direction connecting neuroscience and foundation model development

    Requirements

    Core (essential)

    • BSc/MSc in neuroscience, behavioural sciences, or a related field, with hands-on experimental research experience.

    Basés en plein cœur de Paris, nous faisons bouger l’industrie des jeux en ligne. Nous offrons à nos joueurs une expérience exceptionnelle, à la fois technique, créative et qualitative. Innovation, unité et appartenance : nos valeurs façonnent une culture d’entreprise multiculturelle et unique.
     
    Et si tu avais un futur dans le jeu ?
     
    Techniquement, Winamax c’est :
    • Un moteur de jeu puissant et innovant : adaptation dynamique de l'offre de jeu, parties de poker hautement configurables, détection de fraude
    • Une architecture distribuée et scalable conçue pour traiter en temps réel les flux de la plateforme
    • Une plateforme modulaire soumise à des contraintes de haute disponibilité et de sécurisation des données, capable de gérer de fortes audience

    Contexte
    L'offre de paris sportifs chez Winamax repose sur le traitement en temps réel de flux massifs de données et l'ajustement continu de probabilités. Pour garantir la cohérence entre les cotes et l'exposition financière de Winamax, l'analyse automatisée des mouvements de marché, du volume des mises et des activités atypiques est devenue un enjeu stratégique.
     
    La question à laquelle doit répondre le stage : 
    Comment détecter algorithmiquement les incohérences de probabilités et les volumes atypiques en temps réel pour fournir un Indice de Confiance fiable, capable d'assister la prise de décision ?

    Objectifs du stage
  • Modéliser la cohérence des cotes et un Indice de Confiance : Concevoir des modèles statistiques pour repérer les décalages de probabilités et évaluer en temps réel la fiabilité des activités à fort volume, en croisant la notoriété de l'événement et son historique
  • Intégrer le module au cœur de l'outil trading existant : Développer une brique algorithmique performante qui s'interface directement avec l'application métier des traders, afin d'enrichir leurs outils
  • Validation & mesure de performance (Backtesting) : Tester et calibrer les modèles sur des historiques massifs de données pour maximiser leur précision, minimiser les fausses alertes et mesurer l'impact réel de l'outil sur l'activité

    • Les points d'attention
  • Temps réel et faible latence : capacité à traiter des flux à haute fréquence (milliers d'actualisations et d'activités par seconde) sans ralentir la réactivité des outils
  • Volume de données et backtesting : manipulation de séries temporelles complexes et capacité à tester/ajuster les modèles sur des bases historiques de plusieurs millions de lignes
  • Précision du ciblage (taux de faux positifs) : nécessité d'ajuster finement les seuils statistiques pour remonter des signaux réellement pertinents sans engorger l'outil d'alertes inutiles

    • Stack technique
    Python, Node.js, Sql

    Modalités de stage
  • Stage de fin d'études (Master 2) à pourvoir à temps plein uniquement à Paris, France
  • Opportunité de CDI à la fin du stage
  • Rémunération : 30k

    • Processus de recrutement
  • Test technique
  • Screening RH avec Camille
  • Entretien avec le manager et le maître de stage

    About the role
    In healthcare, the phone is still the front door, and call volume keeps rising while the people answering it are harder to hire and keep.     • Define the enterprise ICP, sales methodology, and a repeatable motion for each segment

    • Build and lead a high-performing enterprise sales team

    • Land and expand with large health systems, health plans, and life sciences companies

    • Lead executive briefings, events, and high-stakes negotiations

    • Collaborative, humble, and driven

    • Passion for the transformative potential of conversational AI

    About the role

    We're hiring a Direct Tax Lead to own our US income tax provision, compliance, and controls, reporting to the Head of Tax. ElevenLabs operates through its US entity and ~9 international entities and is growing fast, which means the provision, the compliance calendar, and the controls around them need a dedicated owner.

    This is a hands-on ownership role. The provision and returns are prepared by external providers; you manage those engagements and are accountable for the output. You'll own the quarterly and annual ASC 740 provision (deferreds, valuation allowance, uncertain tax positions, rate rec, footnote disclosures), the US federal and state compliance calendar (returns, extensions, estimated payments), and the technical work underneath it: §174 capitalization, §382 and NOL tracking.

    • Deep ASC 740 expertise at a multinational — provision, deferreds, valuation allowance, uncertain tax positions, rate reconciliation, and footnote disclosure

    • Experience owning a US federal and multistate compliance calendar (returns, extensions, estimates)

    • Working knowledge of US international provisions (NCTI/GILTI, Subpart F, FDDEI, §163(j)) and how they flow into the provision

    • Experience managing Big 4 or equivalent providers and working directly with external auditors

    • Has built or operated SOX controls over tax, or supported a first SOX implementation

    • CPA

Deine Aufgaben

Als Account Executive (m/w/d) bei Mercanis bist du der zentrale Umsatztreiber für unser bestehendes Kundenportfolio im gehobenen Mittelstand und Enterprise-Segment. Nach unserer erfolgreichen Vertriebs-Restrukturierung trennen wir "Hunting" und "Farming" konsequent: Du übernimmst die volle Vertriebs- und Deal-Verantwortung für ein exklusives Territory von ca. 60–70 bestehenden Accounts.

Deine Mission: Du identifizierst ungenutzte Cross- und Upsell-Potenziale, navigierst souverän durch komplexe C-Level-Buying-Center, steuerst vielschichtige Deal-Zyklen bis zum Verhandlungsabschluss und maximierst so nachhaltig unsere Net Revenue Retention (NRR). Wenn du ein tiefes Verständnis für B2B-SaaS-Vertriebsmethodiken mitbringst und Bestandskunden nicht nur betreuen, sondern durch echten Mehrwert strategisch ausbauen willst, ist dies deine perfekte Gelegenheit.


Dein Aufgabenbereich

  • Expansion & ARR-Wachstum: Du steuerst den gesamten Verkaufszyklus für Upsell-, Cross-Sell- und Modul-Erweiterungen in einem Portfolio von ca. 60–70 Bestandskunden und triffst deine eigenen Quota-Ziele.

  • Pipeline-Generierung im Bestand: Du analysierst deine Accounts eigenständig auf White Spots, identifizierst neue Anwendungsfälle im Bereich Einkauf & Supply Chain Management und generierst aktiv qualifizierte Expansion-Pipeline.

  • Strategisches Closing & C-Level Selling: Du navigierst komplexe Buying Center (CPO, CFO, IT-Leitung), baust Belieber- & Champion-Netzwerke auf Executive-Ebene auf und führst kommerzielle Verhandlungen (Preisgestaltung, Lizenzerweiterungen, Vertragsverlängerungen) eigenständig zum Abschluss.

  • Executive Relationship & Account Planning: Du erstellst strategische Account-Pläne für deine Top-Kunden, führst regelmäßige Business Reviews (QBRs) auf C-Level durch und positionierst Mercanis als unverzichtbaren Software-Partner.

  • Vorhersagbarkeit & Deal Execution: Du steuerst deine Deals anhand etablierter B2B-Sales-Methodiken (z. B. MEDDPICC), pflegst deine Pipeline im CRM mit hoher Forecasting-Genauigkeit und arbeitest eng mit dem Customer Success Team zusammen.


Dein Profil

  • B2B SaaS Closing-Erfahrung: Du bringst nachweisbare Erfolge im B2B-SaaS-Vertrieb (als Account Executive, Enterprise AM oder Senior Closing Role) mit – idealerweise im Umfeld von Procurement-, SCM- oder komplexen B2B-Enterprise-Lösungen.

  • Track Record in Deal Execution: Du hast eine nachweisliche Historie im Erreichen oder Übertreffen deiner Umsatzziele (Quota) und bist vertraut mit komplexen Verkaufszyklen und mehrstufigen Decision-Making-Prozessen.

  • Sales Methodik & Value Selling: Du beherrschst Value-Based Selling, kannst ROI-Analysen auf C-Level überzeugend präsentieren und bist geübt im Umgang mit Sales-Frameworks (z. B. MEDDPICC, SPIN, Challenger).

  • Verhandlungssicherheit & C-Level-Flüssigkeit: Du verhandelst verhandlungssicher auf Deutsch (muttersprachliches Niveau oder seit mindestens 10 Jahren im deutschen Geschäftsumfeld verankert) sowie verhandlungssicher auf Englisch.

  • Präsenz & Skalierungs-Drive: Du wohnst in Berlin (oder bist umzugsbereit) für unser Office-First/Hybrid-Modell, arbeitest datengetrieben und bringst die Motivation mit, in einem schnell skalierenden Tech-Startup Verantwortung zu übernehmen.


Warum wir?

  • Mentoring & persönliches Wachstum: Du arbeitest eng mit erfahrenen Seriengründern zusammen, die dich in deiner fachlichen und persönlichen Entwicklung aktiv begleiten und fördern.
  • Compensation: Kompetitives Fixgehalt + attraktiver, ungedeckelter Bonus & VSOP (Beteiligungsmodell).
  • Perks: Lebe das Scale-up-Life, regelmäßige Team Events & Offsites, und natürlich: kostenlose Uber-Eats-Meals & Uber-Rides, wenn’s mal wieder länger dauert.
  • Room for Ideas: Wir leben eine offene Kultur mit echtem Sparring, du übernimmst Verantwortung und bekommst den Freiraum, deine Ideen voranzutreiben.
  • Team Mindset: Werde Teil eines neugierigen, motivierten Teams, das mutig experimentiert, offen kommuniziert und sich stetig weiterentwickelt, gemeinsam und individuell.
  • Central Location: Unser Büro liegt im Herzen von Berlins Startup-Ökosystem, mit bester Anbindung, großartiger Energie und tollen Menschen.

    Are you a bit tired of the standard, old-fashioned way of doing things in the construction industry? 
    Do you get deep satisfaction from making things run more efficiently using a good dose of common sense and maybe a bit of technology? 
    Have you always cared about the importance of proper planning and the connection between the schedule and the real, day-to-day delivery of the job? 
    Have you ever wanted to work a bit more flexibly but still be hands-on in construction and improving the industry? 
    Sounds like a dream. Well, it isn’t. It’s quite real! Read on. 
    ____________________________________________________________
    We are Laminar Projects!
     
    If you’ve already heard about us, you’re probably reading this because you’re tired of the typical, chaotic ways of doing things in construction. But in case you haven’t, we’re a high-end project management consultancy and tech developer with a focus on upgrading the way construction projects are delivered.
     
    Improving construction strengthens the very foundation of human civilisation. (Check out our short film about it.)
    We bring transparency and control to projects through a pragmatic mix of the latest tech, our own processes, and a big dose of common sense. We then take our deep understanding of these projects and we invest heavily into developing the digital solutions that anyone can use to deliver their projects better. (Check out Shape, our construction management tech, to see what we’re doing.)
     
    The core of all this is our true secret sauce: our people. We only recruit the very best, both in capability and personality. We’re deeply focused on designing a new type of organisation that’s optimised for the flourishing of the people in the team first and foremost. People who join us develop fast as a whole person in ways they never imagined. (Read more about our vision and missions.)
     
    This approach has allowed us to grow from just two people in 2017 to over 220 today. We have a stable, repeat client base across infrastructure and complex building projects in the UK and internationally, and we’re still growing fast. Joining us isn’t just some “job”. It’s a transformative educational experience. We challenge you to be your best self in all aspects of life. There are many diverse and interesting challenges available. It’s up to you to guide yourself into whichever areas you’re most interested – we’ll enable it. 
     
    (Get to know us better by watching a few more of our videos.)
     
    Core values for a good life
     
    A life of human flourishing is all about meaningful relationships and challenging yourself to create a positive impact, so our values reflect the four levels of relationships that each of us has:
     
    - Grow yourself – your relationship with yourself 
    - Care about people – your relationship with others around you 
    - Execute to greatness – your relationship with your team 
    - Build civilisation – your relationship with humanity and the world 
     
    We enshrined our values in our vision:
     
    We exist so that everyone in our team can flourish in a high-impact community that:
     
    - Connects us with meaningful relationships 
    - Inspires us to develop ourselves to become better humans 
    - Empowers us to pursue our own learning adventures 
     
    By first doing this, we can achieve the highest levels of value for the world.
     
    And enable the achievement of our vision through our two missions:
     
    - To fully digitalise the construction of human civilisation 
    - To create a new type of organisation that enables human flourishing while delivering a huge positive impact on society 
    ____________________________________________________________
    The Role 
     
    Purpose of the role 
     
    You’ll be enhancing the delivery of the most complex and interesting projects in the world through the power of project planning to the very highest standards. You’ll devise strategies and tactics to improve the way the project is delivered. You’ll translate this knowledge into a logic-linked plan and analyse it using planning software. Then you’ll use the plan to help the teams understand what to prioritise. 
     
    Your team 
     
    This role is part of our Project Management Consultancy team which focuses on:
     
    - Understanding what the real problems of projects are 
    - Implementing the best solutions to those problems 
    - Developing scalable best practices, tools and technology 
     
    More specifically, you’ll be part of our Project Planning Team, who are industry leaders in the planning of complex construction projects. Your initial leader will be one of our planning discipline directors.
     
    Your top three objectives 
     
    1. To make construction projects deliver to near perfection 
    2. To create scalable and repeatable solutions to common problems 
    3. To develop yourself and everyone around you 
     
    Your top five responsibilities 
     
    1. Own the plan: Own the project plan for one or more projects and ensure that the project is working to it effectively. Ensure delays are mitigated and managed commercially 
    2. Own the outcome: You're responsible for putting in your best effort to ensure the project team’s understanding and focus on the plan – no matter how stubborn they are 
    3. Report and inform: Provide simple, actionable reports to stakeholders at all levels that help them deliver their part of the project more efficiently and effectively 
    4. Make scalable solutions: Develop scalable and repeatable best practices and tools in collaboration with the team so that long-term impact is achieved 
    5. Develop everyone: Maximise the development of your team personally and professionally and educate our clients to improve as well  
     
    You must have:
     
    - A construction engineering background: You have at least 2+ years of experience on construction projects, experience in project planning both software and principles, as well as decent Excel skills, and a strong interest in data
    - Communication skills: You’re proficient in written and verbal English and have the charisma and influence to get construction people to do new things and take the best approach 
    - Leadership capabilities: You lead yourself proactively and lead others by asking the right questions and challenging them 
    - Impact: You have a track record of making projects and organisations better beyond just doing the basics – implementing scalable, repeatable solutions that had a significant positive impact 
     
    Laminar isn’t the place for you if any of the following is true: 
     
    - You want an easy, chilled-out role without much challenge 
    - You like to be the smartest person in the room 
    - You don’t like continuously receiving honest candid feedback 
    - You prefer to do your own thing rather than work with a team
    ____________________________________________________________
    Frequently Asked Questions 
     
    What kinds of projects would I be working on?
    It’s common for people to be exposed to several projects in their first year with us. You’ll work on some of the most complex and interesting environments in the world. We’ve delivered over 100 data centres internationally, many of them fast-tracked and multi-package. Our teams have supported flagship infrastructure programmes like HS2 through integrated planning and digital delivery, contributed to over $30bn in power generation and transmission projects, and played a key role in the development of high-containment labs and R&D campuses for some of the world’s most advanced industrial and life sciences clients. You might find yourself working in sectors such as data centres, infrastructure (including defense, rail, and highways), high tech (such as advanced manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, and semiconductors), or complex building projects. These aren’t hands-off assignments. They’re dynamic, hands-on environments designed for people who want to be challenged. We bring back the lessons from every project to help our team grow and deliver the highest levels of value. (Check out our case stories.) 
     
    Who are our clients?
    Major owners/operators and main contractors with project values between £1m and £1bn+ globally. 
     
    Where would I be working?
    One week you might be working from home. The next, you might travel to the site to meet the construction teams and help organise them. Maybe you’ll pop into our London office for a workshop or a beer. Maybe you’ll fly out to exotic (and sometimes not!) locations in Europe or the Middle East to visit clients. It really depends on what you want to get involved in and what fits with your life. 
     
    How does what I do connect with the long-term impact on the construction industry? 
    You’re tasked with understanding and solving common problems. We don’t want to reinvent the wheel every time, so you’ll be responsible for documenting new solutions and evolving ones we’ve developed. This goes into our knowledge repository, which we’re going to open source to the industry. 
     
    The knowledge you capture will be used by us to build new products. You’ll constantly test those products in the field, so we can rapidly iterate and improve them for anyone in the industry to use. 
     
    ____________________________________________________________
     
    Benefits
     
    The standard stuff: 
     
    - Bonus Scheme. As a permanent member of the team, you’ll share in our success. Our annual bonus is designed to reward both the now and the future - with a flexible mix of cash and high-growth equity that you choose. Bonuses are discretionary and based on performance 
    - Professional body membership. One fee covered per year - so you can stay connected to your field and develop your craft 
     
    The life-changing stuff:
     
    - In-house coaching. Regular 1:1 coaching sessions, fully confidential, to help you navigate challenges, build self-awareness, and grow intentionally - professionally and as a human being
    - Equity upside. As we grow, you grow. Our generous equity scheme is especially powerful for those who stay with us on our journey. You help us build the future - and own a piece of it
    - Flexible working. Work where it makes sense - most of our team works from home, visiting sites or clients regularly. We care about outcomes, not clock-ins
    - Relentless development. Our goal is for every year here to be worth five years of development anywhere else. You’ll get a coach, a mentor, honest feedback, and a culture that challenges you to keep levelling up
    ____________________________________________________________
     
    Important! Applying properly
     
    We get thousands of applications so please write us a letter as part of your application explaining:
     
    - Why you want to join us 
    - What you’ll bring to the team 
     
    We aren't a giant, faceless corporation; we really care about the people who want to join our team, so your letter will be read carefully. After that, we’ll reach out to you to schedule a casual conversation to help you get to know us a bit better and tell us a bit about yourself. A couple of technical and personal assessments follow to understand your capability based on our own development matrix.  
     
    This is to ensure that when you join, you’re starting at the right level of responsibility.

Frequently recognised as an industry leader in supply chain sustainability, RSB applies its best-in-class sustainability framework across sectors including aviation, chemicals, materials, and shipping.

    The Services

    The Sustainable Bio-Materials & Regulatory Compliance Consultant will provide regulatory compliance and sustainability assessment expertise for bio-based materials, sustainable fuels, feedstocks and related value chains. Consultants in this profile support RSB Advisory Services with the expert practical interpretation of regulatory frameworks, such as EU RED, CORSIA and relevant voluntary certification requirements, including their GHG calculation methodologies.     Role purpose: To provide RSB with flexible, project-based technical capacity for assessing whether bio-based materials, fuels, feedstocks and supply chains meet applicable regulatory and voluntary sustainability requirements.     •    Prepare clear GHG, LCA or sustainability assessment reports using agreed templates, including methodology, assumptions, data-quality notes, result presentation and interpretation.

    •    Provide support for the technical understanding of sustainable bio-material pathways and low-ILUC risk considerations under EU RED, CORSIA, RSB or equivalent requirements.

    •    Support regulatory and voluntary-scheme gap analyses by participating in the documentation of benchmarking requirements, identifying, verifying or validating compliance risks, and reviewing third-party organisational documentation against criteria (met, not met or not applicable).

    •    Review certification-readiness documentation under RSB guidance, including evidence related to feedstock origin, traceability, chain of custody, sustainability criteria and GHG claims.

    •    Support the interpretation of policy or regulatory requirements for specific feedstocks, technologies, products or markets by providing supporting data and literature reviews, and translate findings into practical compliance options in line with the applicable standard requirements.

    •    Support the development or refinement of methodologies, blueprints and decision tools for innovative sustainability assessments involving bio-based materials, fuels, chemicals or emerging feedstock pathways.

    •    Strong written and spoken English proficiency.

    •    Strong collaboration and communication skills, the ability to operate autonomously, and a proactive approach to communicating progress, risks, and opportunities in a clear and constructive manner.

    •    Self-sufficiency in a remote and fully digital working environment with reliable internet connectivity. Video calls and collaborative tools will be used for coordination.

     

    Specific to this profile:

    •    Proven hands-on experience applying EU RED, CORSIA, RSB or equivalent GHG and sustainability methodologies in client, certification, policy or project-development contexts.

    •    Working knowledge of at least one major voluntary sustainability certification scheme, preferably RSB, ISCC or another scheme relevant to biofuels, SAF, biomass or bio-based materials.

    •    Ability to work independently with limited onboarding, document assumptions transparently and flag uncertainty, data gaps and compliance risks.

    •    Strong written English and effective reporting skills for technical and non-technical audiences.

    •    Strong communication skills and comfort working with client-provided data under confidentiality constraints.

    •    CET ±5 hours time-zone compatibility, unless otherwise agreed for a specific assignment.

     

    For firms / agencies:

    •    Ability to assign appropriately qualified personnel to assignments and to ensure continuity of delivery, including cover for absences.

    •    Working knowledge of the RSB standard and certification system in particular, or of ISCC.

    •    Hands-on experience using the RSB GHG Calculator.

    •    Experience developing or refining methodologies, blueprints or decision tools for emerging feedstock pathways, bio-based materials, fuels or chemicals.

    Selling outcomes, not capacity

    • The strongest candidates will understand that sophisticated services sales is not about selling consultants, days or technical resources. It is about selling change and business outcomes.

      You will lead discovery around the client’s most important challenges and ambitions, working with Valiantys’ consulting and technical experts to turn those conversations into propositions that have clear strategic relevance and measurable value.

      Whether the opportunity involves enterprise transformation, ITSM/ESM, cloud, DevOps, platform strategy, AI, operating-model change or managed services, you will ensure the conversation begins with the client’s desired outcome, not the technology.

    Orchestrating Valiantys

    • Complex services opportunities are won as a team.

      You will act as the commercial orchestrator for your accounts, bringing together the best of Valiantys across consulting, solution architecture, delivery, customer success, managed services and executive leadership.

      You will create clarity around the client’s ambition, establish a compelling win strategy and ensure our teams are aligned around the outcome we are trying to achieve.

      You will also work closely with Atlassian and our broader partner ecosystem, building strong field relationships and turning platform opportunities into larger transformation and services engagements.

    • Maintain accurate forecasting, qualification and opportunity management throughout the sales cycle.

    • Apply MEDDPICC or a similar methodology to create clarity, momentum and accountability.

    • Contribute to strategic account planning, regional strategy and commercial reporting.

    • Monitor portfolio performance and adjust priorities based on data, market signals and customer engagement.

    • Share insight, best practices and relevant market intelligence with the wider sales organization.

     

    What you need to be successful

    We are looking for a sophisticated enterprise seller with a strong record of building and closing significant consulting and professional services business with more than 10 years of experience minimum. 

    You will bring most of the following:

    • Evidence of consistently delivering against ambitious services revenue and bookings targets.

    • Strong experience growing strategic accounts and creating substantial new revenue within existing client relationships.

    • The ability to engage credibly with C-suite and senior executive stakeholders, combining commercial confidence with intellectual curiosity.

    • The ability to move comfortably between strategic business conversations and the commercial detail required to get complex deals signed.

    • Experience creating opportunities where no formal requirement or RFP previously existed.

    • Strong commercial judgment across pricing, scope, margin, contracting, negotiation and deal structure.

    • The ability to navigate complex organizations, political environments and multi-stakeholder buying processes.

    • Experience orchestrating multidisciplinary teams around large pursuits.

    • Strong forecasting, pipeline management and opportunity qualification discipline.

    • Experience within technology consulting, digital transformation, enterprise service management, ITSM, cloud, DevOps, AI transformation or the Atlassian ecosystem would be highly valuable.

    • Strong collaboration skills and the ability to align consultants, delivery teams, partners and executives around a shared opportunity.

    If you are ready to develop strategic accounts, achieve ambitious goals, and make a real impact, we would love to hear from you.
     

    Why Valiantys?

    Valiantys is a fast-growing, international and entrepreneurial organization at the intersection of technology, consulting and business transformation. You will work with experienced specialists who care about the quality of the outcome—not just the signature of the contract.

    What we offer

    • An international, multicultural team and a genuinely European scope.

    • A flexible telework program.

    • Personal dental plan and health insurance fully funded by Valiantys.

    • Choice of PC or Mac.

    • Training time and budget to support your development.

    Ready to create momentum?

    If you are looking for a role where you can combine enterprise selling, strategic thinking and real customer impact, we would like to hear from you.

    Whether your strength is expanding strategic accounts or opening new enterprise relationships, you will have the opportunity to shape markets, build meaningful partnerships and directly influence the growth of Valiantys and our customers.

    Great salespeople create opportunities. Exceptional ones create momentum.
